brief:
Today, 1 November, is Pull A at the New York gym, and tomorrow is Legs A. The app's six-day order would have said Pull B, but you did Pull B on 29 October; Pull A and Legs A are the two nights that have not run here, and Pull A goes first so that your second leg night comes 72 hours after 30 October, not 48. You have trained four nights in four days, so if tonight is a rest day, that is a fair call: then Pull A tomorrow and Legs A the day after.

First, the dips. You were right: the Push B card on 31 October had two dips lifts on it. Here is why. When you type a name on a card, the app keeps that name for that slot at this gym on every night. On 28 October you did dips in the Push A triceps slot and named the card Dips, so on 31 October the same slot came up on Push B as Dips, next to the program's own Assisted Dips. The program itself had one dips slot; the card showed two. From today there is one dips slot and it is on Push A, where you did them: three sets of 8 to 12 bar dips at bodyweight, leaning forward, finishing the chest night. Push B loses its dips slot and keeps the machine chest press as its flat press (three sets of 8 to 10; it was 135 for 12s on Push A on 28 October). The smith bench you did instead, 185 for 8, 8, 8, is not added: one night, done in anger at the card, on a smith machine that was already taken on 30 October; if you want it in place of the machine press on Push B, write that in a note and it becomes the slot. The overhead cable extension leaves both nights: at New York it was never done as itself (dips on 28 October, a rope pushdown on 31 October), so its Push B slot is now the rope pushdown you did, three sets of 10 to 12 from 47.5. Push B goes from 23 sets to 20, nearer the 17 you have been finishing; Push A stays at 19; chest stays at 18 sets a week. The same name rule means the Legs B squat card now says Leg Extension, the Push B last card says Overhead db press and the Push A lateral-raise card says Db lateral raise; blank the name field on a card to get the program's lift back.

What this week showed on your first New York nights: shoulder press 45 lb dumbbells for 8, 10, 10, 10, four sets in range and 10 lb under your Chennai 25 kg, so next Push B is 50 for 10s. Leg press 160, 180, 200 for 10, 10, 8 (typed in afterwards, within 12 seconds). Leg extension 150 then 157.5 for 10 in the squat slot because the smith was taken; so the gym has one, which answers the question I had dated 6 November. Leg curl 120, 135, 150 for 10, logged live. Cable crunch 52.5 for 12, 10, 10. Ab wheel 8, 8. Lateral raise 15 for 15, 13, 13. Crossover 29 for 15, 13. Rope pushdown 42.5 then 47.5 for 12, 12, 10. The two sets you logged as Overhead db press, 50 for 12, 12, read as an overhead dumbbell triceps extension (one 50 lb dumbbell, two hands); that fits the slot, and it becomes the slot the next time you do it there. The RDL and the calf press were skipped on 30 October in a 29-minute night, and the reverse pec deck was skipped on Push B for the second time in three Push B nights; one more skip there and it comes off Push B.

Tonight, Pull A, 21 sets, every number in pounds. Deadlift: 235 for 5, four sets (you pulled 235 for 5, 5, 5 at Vancouver on 23 October; tonight adds the fourth set, and all four at 5 earns 245). Wide-grip pulldown: 105 for 10, then 120 for 8, 8; this stack is new to you, and your 28 August night at the old home gym was 135 then 150, so if 105 is clearly easy go to 135 and log it. Seated cable row: 105 for 12, four sets; 115 if it is easy. Dumbbell curl: 30 lb for 9, three sets, one rep more than Vancouver, same weight. Cable hammer curl: 35 for 12, three sets. Face pulls: 32.5 for 12 to 15, two sets, up from the 27.5 you did for 15, 15 on 29 October (30 if the stack has it). Cable lateral raise: 10 for 12, two sets, light and strict; this is the slot added on 26 October and tonight is its first night. Stop each set with two or three reps left; this is still week one on these machines.

Tomorrow, Legs A: leg press 180 for 10 then 200 for 8, 8; split squat 20 lb for 10 each leg, two sets; leg curl 135 for 10 then 150 for 10, 10; leg extension 150 for 12, two sets; adductor 80 and abductor 60 for 12, two sets each, as starting points (your August home-gym machines took 105 and 135; if these read like that, go there on the first set); calf press on the leg press 250 for 12, three sets, the slot that has been skipped twice and is decided on 3 November; cable crunch 52.5 for 12, three sets. Tomorrow's review will carry those as the card numbers.

Still open: whether this New York gym is the one you trained at in August. Your 29 October pulldown, straight-arm, shrug and face-pull numbers match your 25 August night to the pound, so where it costs nothing the August numbers are quoted above as the place to go if a first set is easy; it is not assumed, because the log cannot prove it. And no bodyweight has been logged since 23 August (207 lb); a morning weigh-in this week would anchor the block.

flags.note: Tonight is Pull A, not the rotation’s Pull B (which ran on 29 October); Legs A is tomorrow, so the second leg night lands 72 hours after 30 October, not 48.

The push nights changed today from what you did and wrote this week: one dips slot, on Push A; Push B loses its dips slot and keeps the machine chest press; the overhead cable extension leaves both nights and its Push B slot becomes the rope pushdown; Push B is 20 sets, down from 23.

A name you type on a card sticks to that slot at this gym on every night: the Push B card showed two dips cards on 31 October because the overhead slot was named Dips on 28 October; the Legs B squat card now reads Leg Extension, the Push B last card reads Overhead db press and the Push A lateral card reads Db lateral raise until you blank the name field.
Four nights in four days (28 to 31 October); a rest day tonight is a fair call, and then Pull A tomorrow and Legs A the day after.

The calf press has been skipped at Chennai and at New York on 30 October; tomorrow’s Legs A is the last read before the decision on 3 November, so do it, or write in the note what calf machine the gym has instead.

The leg extension question is answered early: the gym has one (150 and 157.5 for 10 on 30 October in the squat slot), so the slot stays; when the smith is taken, the leg extension stands in for the squat.
The two sets logged as Overhead db press, 50 for 12, 12, in the Push B reverse-grip slot read as an overhead dumbbell triceps extension; the slot becomes that lift the next time you do it there.
No bodyweight logged since 23 August (207 lb); a morning weigh-in this week would anchor the block.

block.why: Meso 3 restarted on 28 October at the New York gym (build to 24 November, deload 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December; the show is 120 days away). Four nights in four days since: Push A on 28 October (18 of 19 sets, typed in from memory), Pull B on 29 October (20 of 21, logged live), Legs B on 30 October (14 of 20 in 29 minutes: the RDL and the calf press skipped, the smith taken so the squat slot became a leg extension; the leg press and the first two extension sets typed in seconds apart, the curl, rollout and crunch live), Push B on 31 October (17 of 23 in 52 minutes: the chest press and reverse pec deck skipped, a smith bench in the dips slot with a note, two triceps slots done as other lifts). Pull A and Legs A still have no New York night; they are tonight and tomorrow, in that order, so the second leg night lands 72 hours after the first rather than 48. The block is doing what week one of a build should on the lifts that ran: every Pull B lift sits in its rep range, the leg curl took 150 for 10 logged live, the shoulder press went four sets in range. One structural change today, at the week level: the two push nights were near-copies (same chest press, same reverse pec deck, same overhead extension, a crossover each), and the 31 October note said the card had two dips lifts on it, which it did: the name typed on the overhead slot on 28 October (“Dips”) sticks to that slot at this gym on every night. So: one dips slot, on Push A, under the bar-dip id; Push B loses its dips slot and keeps the machine chest press as its flat press; the overhead cable extension, never done as itself at New York, leaves both nights, and its Push B slot becomes the rope pushdown you did. Push A stays 19 sets, Push B goes 23 to 20, chest stays 18 a week, direct triceps sets go 11 to 8 (the floor) with four pressing lifts behind them. The smith bench is not added: it was done once, in anger at the card, on a smith machine that was already taken on 30 October; it becomes the slot if you ask. Tonight: Pull A, the first New York deadlift, 235 for 5 on four sets. Four days straight also makes a rest day tonight a fair call; if so, Pull A tomorrow and Legs A the day after, and the calves date moves with the leg night. Open and dated: calves on 3 November, the counting-rule mismatch behind nine muscles that read over their ceilings on 9 November. Watched without a date: the Push B reverse pec deck (skipped two of three), the fourth shrug set, the Push A lateral-raise slot, the reverse-grip slot (read as an overhead dumbbell extension, 50 for 12s). The next boundary is the deload on 25 November: sets drop to about 60% and loads by 20%, and the prep block is written at the assessment from what these four weeks log.

chest.why: Eighteen direct sets a rotation after today’s push-day change (Push A: incline 4, chest press 3, crossover 3, dips 3; Push B: chest press 3, crossover 2), exactly the ceiling of 18 and the same count as before; what moved is that the one dips slot is now on Push A, where you did dips on 28 October, and off Push B, where you refused them on 31 October. Push A is the chest-led night with 13 and Push B the shoulder-led night with 5, on purpose. 10 a week done over four weeks. New York chest nights so far: 28 October (incline 175 for 6, chest press 135 for 12, crossover 12.5 for 12s, typed in from memory) and 31 October (a smith bench 185 for 8, 8, 8 in the dips slot and the high-to-low crossover 29 for 15, 13, logged live; the machine chest press skipped).

front-delts.why: Eight direct sets (incline press 4, Push B shoulder press 4), inside the direct range of 4 to 10; the 15 on paper is those 8 plus half a set from every chest press and the dips, which is the counting question dated 9 November. The shoulder press ran at New York on 31 October: 45 lb dumbbells for 8, 10, 10, 10, four sets in range, logged live, 10 lb under the 25 kg (55 lb) you pressed for 8 and 9 at Chennai on 15 October, so the block opened a step light and has room to climb.

side-delts.why: Eight direct sets a rotation (Push A raise 3, Push B dumbbell raise 3, the Pull A cable raise 2 added on 26 October) plus half credit from the Push B press, 10 on paper, against a floor of 8 direct. 5.1 a week done over four weeks. At New York: the Push A slot ran as dumbbell lateral raises on 28 October (12.5 for 12s, typed in), and the Push B dumbbell raise ran on 31 October, 15 lb for 15, 13, 13, logged live. The Pull A cable raise gets its first night tonight. Watching, not changing, until all three slots have a New York night.

rear-delts.why: Ten direct sets (reverse pec deck 3 and 3, face pulls 2 and 2), inside the direct range of 6 to 12; the 15.5 on paper is half credit from every pulldown and row (dated 9 November). 6.4 a week done over four weeks. The Push A pec deck ran on 28 October, 90 for 13, 12, 12. The Push B pec deck was skipped on 31 October and on 15 October at Chennai, two of the last three Push B nights; in the new Push B it sits fifth of seven on a night that is now 20 sets instead of 23, so it gets one more Push B before it is judged: skipped again and it comes off Push B, with the two face-pull slots going to three sets each.

lats.why: Seventeen direct sets on paper (wide pulldown 3, seated row 4, chest-supported row 4, close pulldown 3, straight-arm 3), 18 with the rollout’s half credit, at the ceiling of 18. 8.5 a week done over four weeks. Pull B ran at New York on 29 October (close pulldown 112.5 for 10 then 127.5 for 9, 9; straight-arm 45 for 9 then 37.5 for 10, 10; chest-supported row 50 for 8s). Pull A gets its first New York night tonight.

upper-back.why: Eight direct sets (seated row 4, chest-supported dumbbell row 4), the floor of the direct range 8 to 16; the 19.5 on paper is half credit from every pulldown, deadlift, shrug and face pull (dated 9 November). 8 a week done over four weeks. The chest-supported row had its first night on 29 October, 50 lb a hand for 8, 8, 8, 8. The seated row runs tonight.

traps.why: Four direct shrug sets planned since 26 October, the direct floor of 4; the rest of the 9.5 on paper is half credit from the deadlift, face pulls and lateral raises. The first night of four sets, 29 October, ran three: 80 lb dumbbells for 15, 15, 15. 3.5 a week done over four weeks. No Pull B since, so nothing new: if the next Pull B also stops at three, the fourth set comes off rather than staying on paper.

lower-back.why: No direct slot: the 3.5 on paper is half credit from the deadlift (4) and the barbell RDL (3). Held without a direct lift on purpose; a heavy deadlift and a barbell RDL in the same week are the lower-back work. The RDL was skipped on 30 October, so the lower back has had nothing since Vancouver’s deadlift on 23 October and comes to tonight’s deadlift fresh.

biceps.why: Eleven direct sets (dumbbell curl 3, hammer 3, incline curl 2, reverse curl 3), inside the direct range of 8 to 14; the 18 on paper adds half a set from each pull (dated 9 November). 8.9 a week done over four weeks. Pull B curls at New York on 29 October: incline curl 25 for 10 then 30 for 9, reverse curl 27.5 then 32.5 for 10, 10, 10. The Pull A curls run tonight.

triceps.why: Eight direct sets after today’s change (dips 3 on Push A, rope pushdown 3 and reverse-grip pushdown 2 on Push B), the floor of the direct range 8 to 14, down from 11 because the two overhead-extension slots became dips (which count for chest too) and a rope pushdown, and the Push B dips slot is gone; the 16.5 on paper adds half a set from the incline, two chest presses, the shoulder press and the straight-arm pulldown, which is why it still reads over the ceiling (dated 9 November). 12.3 a week done over four weeks, the best-served muscle in the log by that count, so eight direct sets plus four pressing lifts is enough for now. What you did at New York: dips 8, 10, 12 on 28 October; rope pushdown 42.5 for 12 then 47.5 for 12, 10 on 31 October; and two sets logged as “Overhead db press”, 50 for 12, 12, in the reverse-grip slot, which read as an overhead dumbbell triceps extension (see that lift).

forearms.why: Six direct sets (hammer and reverse curls), inside the direct range of 2 to 8; the 12 on paper adds half a set from the dumbbell curl, the shrugs, the pushdown and the rows (dated 9 November). 5.5 a week done over four weeks. Reverse curl 32.5 for 10s on 29 October; the hammer curl runs tonight.

quads.why: Thirteen direct sets a rotation (Legs A press 3, split squat 2, leg extension 2; Legs B smith squat 3, feet-low press 3), inside 10 to 18, unchanged. 3.1 a week done over four weeks, the most under-served muscle in the log, and 30 October was the first quad night since 14 October: leg press 160, 180, 200 for 10, 10, 8 (all three typed in within 12 seconds, so recalled) and leg extension 150, 157.5, 157.5 for 10 in the squat slot because the smith was taken (the first two typed 7 seconds apart). Legs A is tomorrow, 72 hours after that night, rather than tonight at 48 hours with the soreness yesterday’s review warned about.

hamstrings.why: Thirteen direct sets (deadlift 4, barbell RDL 3, two leg curls 6), inside 8 to 14; the 15.5 on paper adds half credit from the split squat and smith squat (dated 9 November). 6.1 a week done over four weeks. Leg curl at New York on 30 October: 120, 135, 150 for 10, 10, 10, logged live, the first New York hamstring work. The RDL was skipped that night, so the hinge has not run here yet; tonight’s deadlift is the first.

glutes.why: Twelve direct sets (deadlift 4, split squat 2, RDL 3, smith squat 3), inside 6 to 14; the 16 on paper adds half credit from two leg presses and the abductor (dated 9 November). 5.5 a week done over four weeks. Neither the RDL nor the smith squat ran on 30 October (skipped; smith taken), so the only glute work at New York is half credit from the leg press. Tonight’s deadlift and tomorrow’s split squat are the first real glute nights here.

adductors.why: Two direct sets on Legs A, the floor of 2 to 6; the 7.5 on paper adds half credit from the leg presses, smith squat and split squat, which is why it reads over the ceiling (dated 9 November). 1.9 a week done over four weeks. Tomorrow is the first New York night for the adductor machine: 80 for 12 is the starting point from Singapore’s 80 for 15 on 5 October; the August home-gym machine took 105 for 12s on 20 August, and if this stack reads like that, go there on the first set.

abductors.why: Two planned, exactly the floor, all on Legs A. Last 60 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October; skipped at Chennai on 14 October. Tomorrow is the first New York night: 60 for 12 is the starting point, the same rule as the adductor (the last machine logged); the August home-gym machine took 135 for 13s on 20 August, so if this stack reads like that, go there on the first set.

calves.why: Six direct sets a rotation (calf press on the leg press, 3 on Legs A and 3 on Legs B), exactly the floor of 6. 1.9 a week done over four weeks, and still no calf work since Singapore on 5 October (290 for 15, 12 then 270 for 14): the Legs B calf press was skipped on 30 October, in a 29-minute night that also skipped the RDL at the start, so this reads as a short night rather than a missing machine. Tomorrow’s Legs A carries the slot again. Dated in deferred[] to 3 November, the morning after that leg night: logged and the slot stays on both leg nights; skipped again and it moves earlier in both leg nights or becomes the standing or seated calf machine this gym has, with your note on which exists; no leg night by then and the date moves with it. It does not go without a replacement.

abs.why: Eight planned (cable crunch 3 and 3, ab wheel rollout 2). 3.3 a week done over four weeks. Both ran on 30 October at New York, logged live: ab wheel 8, 8 from the knees on its first night, cable crunch 52.5 for 12, 10, 10 on this stack. Tomorrow’s Legs A crunch holds 52.5 and chases 12 on all three.

smith-incline-press.why: On 28 October at New York: 155, 175, 175 for 6 each, typed in within 11 seconds at the start of a 10-minute logging window, so remembered, not logged set by set; three sets, not the four asked. No Push A since. Hold 175 for 6 on the next Push A, all four sets, logged as you go; a rep gain on four logged sets earns the next step. The August home-gym incline was also 175 (175 for 8s on 17 August). Whether New York is the gym you trained at in August is still not in the log, so August numbers are quoted, not prescribed.

machine-chest-press.why: First New York night 28 October on Push A: 105, 120, 135 for 12 each, typed in within 11 seconds, so remembered. On 31 October the Push B slot was skipped and a smith bench done in the dips slot instead (185 for 8s), so this press has one New York night on one of its two days. It stays on both: Push A 10 to 12 (hold 135 for 12, three straight sets, logged as you go), Push B 8 to 10 (first New York night still to come; open at 135 and find the 8-to-10 weight). If you would rather the smith bench on Push B, say so in a note and the slot becomes it.

machine-lateral-raise.why: In the program since 13 October and never once done as itself: on 28 October the slot ran as dumbbell lateral raises, 12.5 lb for 12, 12, 12 (typed in within 1.3 seconds), and that name now sits on this card at New York until you blank it. Whether the gym has a lateral raise machine is not in the log. If the next Push A is dumbbells again, the slot becomes what you actually do; since Push B already has the dumbbell raise (15 for 15, 13, 13 on 31 October), it would become a cable raise or a different angle, not a duplicate.

reverse-pec-deck.why: Push A on 28 October at New York: 90 for 13, 12, 12, logged live. Push B on 31 October: skipped, as it was at Chennai on 15 October, two of the last three Push B nights (12 October it was 50 kg for 11s). The dossier calls it stalled; that is arithmetic across four gyms’ machines. Hold 90 on Push A and chase 15s. On Push B, now 20 sets with this fifth of seven, it gets one more chance; skipped again and it comes off Push B.

chest-dip.why: In the program from today as the one dips slot, on Push A where you did bar dips on 28 October (8, 10, 12 at bodyweight, in the overhead-extension slot, no note). Earlier bar dips: 10, 10, 10 at Warsaw on 30 September, 8, 10 on 22 September; bench dips ran 17 to 19 at the home gym and Chennai. Three sets of 8 to 12 bar dips, chest lean; next Push A 10, 10, 10, and 12 on all three earns a slower tempo or added weight. This is the catalogue’s bar-dip id, chosen because the old dips id carries the name you typed on it at New York on 31 October (“Smith bench”) and would have shown that name on the Push A card.

assisted-dips.why: Off the program today: it was the Push B dips slot, and on 31 October you wrote on it that you had two dips cards and did a smith bench press instead, 185 for 8, 8, 8. Its history as dips: 12s at the home gym in July and August, bench dips 15 to 19 on 14 September, bar dips 10s at Warsaw on 30 September, bench dips 17s at Chennai on 12 October, skipped on 15 October. Dips continue on Push A under the bar-dip id.

overhead-cable-triceps.why: Out of the program today on both push nights. At New York it was never done as itself: dips in the Push A slot on 28 October, a rope pushdown in the Push B slot on 31 October (42.5 for 12, then 47.5 for 12, 10). Before that, skullcrushers on 12 October and an overhead extension at Chennai on 15 October (45 for 13, 15). The last true cable overhead extension was Singapore on 6 October, 115 for 12. Four push nights running the card asked for one lift and got another; the slots become what you do. It comes back if you ask.

Then 255 for 3s on 20 September (early morning), 225 at Singapore on 8 October (sick), and 235 for 5, 5, 5 at Vancouver on 23 October, three sets, not four. Tonight, the first New York deadlift, with the lower back fresh (the RDL was skipped on 30 October): 235 for 5 on all four sets; all four earns 245.

On this gym’s stack the close-grip pulldown took 127.5 for 9 on 29 October, and the 28 August home-gym night on this lift was 135 then 150 for 10, 7. Tonight opens at 105 for 10 then 120 for 8, 8; if 105 is clearly easy on this stack, go to 135 and log it.

cable-hammer-curl.why: Vancouver on 23 October: 37.5 for 10, 10, 10 on a different stack; Singapore 36 for 12s; the 28 August home-gym night 35 for 12s. No New York number yet. Tonight starts at 35 for 12, three sets, a step under Vancouver on a stack you have not logged.

face-pulls.why: 29 October on Pull B at New York, logged live: 27.5 for 15, 15, the top of the 12 to 15 range on both sets, the same 27.5 for 15, 15 as 3 September and 28 August at the home gym; Vancouver’s 22.5 for 14s was a different stack. The dossier’s stall flag is fair: two months at 27.5. Top of the range on both sets earns the step on this stack: tonight 32.5 for 12 to 15, two sets (30 if the stack has it).

Tomorrow sets the New York number: 80 for 12, two sets, as a starting point from the last machine logged; if this stack reads like August, go to 105 on the first set and log it.

Dumbbells read the same anywhere, and Chennai on 15 October was 25 kg (55 lb) for 8 and 9, so you opened the block 10 lb light and finished three sets at the top of the range.
